"'''Baby Don't Get Hooked on Me'''" is a hit song by [[country music|country]] and [[pop music|pop]] singer-songwriter [[Mac Davis]]. From his breakthrough album of the same name, the song reached No.1 on both the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and [[Hot Adult Contemporary|Easy Listening]] charts in September 1972, spending three weeks atop each chart. ''Billboard'' ranked it as the [[Billboard Year-End Hot 100 singles of 1972|No. 8 song of 1972]]. Davis wrote it when the record company demanded he write a tune with a "hook".<ref name="americansongwriter.com">{{cite web|last=Sharp |first=Ken |url=https://americansongwriter.com/mac-davis-hook-line-and-sinker/ |title=MAC DAVIS: Hook, Line and Sinker « American Songwriter |website=Americansongwriter.com |date=2009-01-02 |accessdate=2020-10-01}}</ref>

The song was also a modest country hit concurrent with its pop success, reaching No. 26 shortly after the peak of that success in the pop realm. It was featured on an episode of ''[[The Muppet Show]]'' that Mac Davis was hosting.

"Baby Don't Get Hooked on Me" is a hit song by country and pop singer-songwriter Mac Davis. From his breakthrough album of the same name, the song reached No.1 on both the Billboard Hot 100 and Easy Listening charts in September 1972, spending three weeks atop each chart. Billboard ranked it as the No. 8 song of 1972. Davis wrote it when the record company demanded he write a tune with a "hook".

The song was also a modest country hit concurrent with its pop success, reaching No. 26 shortly after the peak of that success in the pop realm. It was featured on an episode of The Muppet Show that Mac Davis was hosting.
